questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Urgent activities are those things / that you must do immediately, / as they require quick action / and cannot be put on.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **and cannot be put on**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the fourth part of the given sentence, the phrase 'put on' is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be 'put off', which means to delay or postpone something.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be used in place of the incorrect one.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Urgent activities are those things that you must do immediately, as they require quick action and cannot be **put off**.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The meeting / will taking / place next / Wednesday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'will taking' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the verb form 'taking' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be **'will take'** to match the future tense.
 
• The verb **'will'** should be followed by the **base form **of the** verb**, which is** 'take' **in this context.
 
• **Example:** *The meeting will take place next Wednesday.*

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *The meeting will take place next Wednesday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When constructing sentences in the future tense, always ensure that the modal 'will' is followed by the base form of the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** *She will go to the market tomorrow.*
 
 
 
• This rule applies to all subjects, whether singular or plural.
 
 
• Example: *They will arrive at the station soon.*
